findings.title: NPE risk: getResourceTypeResource can return null and is passed directly to findByResource
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String) the fallback path does `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and then immediately calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the resource server is not the admin-permissions client, when admin permissions are disabled for the realm, or simply when no resource named "Clients" exists in the store (which is the case for any realm whose admin-permissions client was initialized before this resource type was added to the schema, since AdminPermissionsSchema.init() only creates the type resources on first creation). Passing a null Resource to findByResource will throw a NullPointerException (or a store-level error) during an authorization check, turning permission evaluation into a 500 error instead of a deny. The result of getResourceTypeResource must be null-checked before use.

findings.title: Existence of a per-client resource silently disables the all-clients permission fallback
findings.body: hasPermission(client, scope) only falls back to the "Clients" resource-type resource when no resource exists for the specific client. But a resource for a client is created as a side effect of ANY scope permission referencing that client, even one that grants the current admin nothing (e.g. a permission created by/for a different administrator). From that point on, evaluation only considers the per-client resource and the all-clients (resource-type) permission is ignored entirely. Consequence: an administrator who was granted e.g. MANAGE or VIEW on all clients via a resource-type permission will be wrongly denied access to any client that has any per-client permission defined, contradicting canManage()/canView() realm-wide semantics and the V1 behavior where realm-level and per-object permissions are combined. There is also no test covering the combination of an all-clients permission with a per-client permission for Clients, so this regression is unguarded.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal "Clients" as a client ID
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission(scope) iterates all resources of type CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE and adds resource.getName() to the result set. This includes the resource-type-level resource named "Clients" (created in AdminPermissionsSchema.init with type "Clients"), so when an all-clients permission grants the requested scope, the string "Clients" is added to a set that callers treat as a set of client IDs. Any caller doing a client lookup or membership check with these IDs will fail to resolve "Clients", producing wrong filtering (e.g. an admin with an all-clients map-roles permission getting an empty/bogus list of clients they can map roles for). The type-level resource must be excluded from the collected names (and ideally the caller informed that all clients are granted).

findings.title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException and can surface as HTTP 500 in the token exchange flow
findings.body: canExchangeTo(ClientModel, ClientModel, AccessToken) is part of the authorization evaluation API used by the token exchange code path to decide whether exchange into a target client is allowed. Overriding it to throw UnsupportedOperationException means that, in realms with ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, any code path that still calls this method will fail with an unhandled exception (HTTP 500 on a token request) rather than a proper deny (returning false) or a clean 4xx. The same applies to the other evaluation-adjacent overrides (isPermissionsEnabled, getPermissions, resource). If these are intentionally unsupported in V2 they should return a safe default or the endpoints/call sites should be feature-gated so they are never reached under V2, not blow up at runtime.

findings.title: registerListener guards on the V1 feature flag but management() dispatches to V2, causing exceptions or missing cleanup
findings.body: The listener now only runs when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled, but AdminPermissions.management() returns a MgmtPermissionsV2 (and thus ClientPermissionsV2) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled. Two problems follow: (1) if both features are enabled at once (nothing prevents `--features=admin-fine-grained-authz,admin-fine-grained-authz-v2`), the ClientRemovedEvent handler calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which ClientPermissionsV2 overrides to throw UnsupportedOperationException — the exception fires inside the client-removal event listener and can abort client deletion with a 500. (2) with V2-only, no cleanup happens at all, so per-client authorization resources in the admin-permissions resource server are orphaned when a client is deleted, accumulating stale resources that keep being returned by getClientsWithPermission. The guard and the dispatch target use different feature flags and need to be reconciled.

findings.title: No migration path: existing admin-permissions realms lack the Clients resource and the new scopes
findings.body: AdminPermissionsSchema.init() returns early when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, so it only creates the schema resources/scopes at first enablement. A realm that enabled admin permissions before this change has only the "Users" resource and the scopes manage/view/impersonate/map-roles/manage-group-membership. After this change, such a realm has no "Clients" resource and no configure/map-roles-client-scope/map-roles-composite scopes, so creating any client permission referencing those scopes fails with "Scope [x] does not exist", and getResourceTypeResource for "Clients" returns null (which then triggers the NPE described for ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission). Even if the V2 feature is preview and migration is not guaranteed, either a migration/upgrade step or a lazy re-sync of schema resources and scopes on realm load is needed, otherwise previously working realms break on upgrade.

findings.title: getResourceName not updated for the Clients resource type, returning null display names
findings.body: getResourceName resolves user resources to a username and special-cases the "Users" all-resource as "All users", but no branch was added for the new CLIENTS resource type. For per-client resources, which are auto-created in getOrCreateResource with name = client's internal ID and no display name, the method falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which is null. Any consumer of getResourceName (e.g. building policy/permission representations for the admin UI) will render null instead of a client name/clientId for client permissions, and the "Clients" all-resource will show its raw type name instead of a friendly label like "All clients".
